requirement:
Give `search_structure` the language, an ast-grep rule, and an optional match limit. Each match carries a node reference for `read_node` and a tag for `finish_search`.
For the `instructions` field, see {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`.

```text
search_structure({language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer})
  -> {search_id: UUID, instructions?: string, next?: UUID, complete: boolean, matches: {tag: string, node: NodeId, excerpt: string}[]}
```
rationale:
The structural assessment finds the `search_structure` signature and result shape in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_structure.mcp` fully supported.

**Input signature `{language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer}`**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` declares the `search_structure` tool.
  - `language` is a string and `rule` is an object.
  - Both are `required`.
  - `limit` is an optional integer with `minimum` 0.
- `#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[dispatch]`, in its `"search_structure"` arm, enforces the schema.
  - It requires `rule` to be an object and `language` to be a string.
  - It parses `limit` as an optional nonnegative integer through `optional_number`.
  - It builds a `StructuralQuery` with that limit.

**Result `{search_id, instructions?, next?, complete, matches: {tag, node, excerpt}[]}`**
- The `dispatch` arm turns each hit into an entry `{node, excerpt}`.
  - `node` is the serialized node reference.
  - `excerpt` is `hit.item.redacted_span(hit.span)`.
- It pairs each entry with a `Dependency::Node` observation and passes the entries and `found.complete` to `pages.search`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/pages.rs#impl[Pages<N,%20L>]/fn[search]` builds each page as `{search_id, complete, matches}`.
  - It adds a `tag` to every match, numbered per page, and records the tag in the stored `SearchPage` entries so `finish_search` can resolve it.
  - It adds `instructions` only to the first page of the first search, when `self.searches` is empty and the index is 0. This matches the optional `instructions?` field and the cited `first_search.instructions` rule.
  - It adds `next` (a UUID) on pages that have a following page.
  - It returns a page even when the result is empty.
- `read_node` consumes the node reference, so that part of the contract is carried by the `node` field of each match.

**Gaps**
- None found within the structural scope.
- The `search_structure` arm of `dispatch` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/sources.rs` is a separate tool surface that takes a `prefix` and uses `read_source`. It is not an implementation root for this requirement.
- No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply.
- Behavioral and test evidence is outside this structural check. I saw no test marked `{test}` for `.mcp`, but this assessment did not judge test adequacy.

text: Give `search_structure` the language, an ast-grep rule, and an optional match limit. Each match carries a node reference for `read_node` and a tag for `finish_search`.
search_structure({language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer})
-> {search_id: UUID, instructions?: string, next?: UUID, complete: boolean, matches: {tag: string, node: NodeId, excerpt: string}[]}
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
